title: Verifier‑Assisted vs. LLM‑Only Pre‑deployment Network‑Change Validation: A Confirmatory Paired Study
abstract: We evaluated whether adding a deterministic pre‑deployment verifier to an LLM‑driven change‑generation workflow increases the fraction of intent‑driven configuration proposals that pass semantic validation (unflagged verifier pass) compared with accepting a single LLM candidate. Under a preregistered paired design (cnsmp2026-llm-verifier-predeployment-001; preregistration SHA‑256 = 425cb1652354120cf48f686b964723d64c76d0a8abe53cd5b5ad0eaa1af71fc7) we executed 300 paired intents (100 per complexity stratum) using gpt-5-mini and a deterministic NetOps validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5). A single shared LLM generation was produced per pair and then evaluated under two conditions: baseline = accept single‑shot output; guarded = validator + up to one automated repair. Results (analysis/condition_summary.csv): baseline 299/300 unflagged passes (0.9966667), guarded 300/300 (1.0); paired contingency n11=299, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0; absolute paired difference = 0.0033333; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; 95% paired bootstrap percentile CI = [0.00, 0.01] (bootstrap_seed=1729, B=10000). The preregistered target effect (10 percentage points) was not observed due to near‑ceiling baseline performance on this synthetic suite. We report the frozen design, execution accounting (planned 600 episodes, completed 600, model_calls_used=301, repair stage_counts=1), full analysis, and discuss construct and external validity implications for assessing verifier utility under more challenging, diverse conditions.

sections.introduction: Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly applied to NetOps problems such as intent→configuration translation, template synthesis, and automated repair. Prior work indicates that augmenting LLMs with external tools—particularly deterministic validators—can reduce syntactic and semantic errors, motivating integration of verifiers in pre‑deployment workflows. However, the marginal benefit of a verifier depends on base model quality, task difficulty, and validator coverage. We preregistered and executed a confirmatory paired experiment to measure that marginal effect under a controlled synthetic NetOps suite. Research question: Does a verifier‑assisted pipeline increase the fraction of change proposals that pass semantic pre‑deployment validation (unflagged) compared with single‑shot LLM generation? Contributions: (1) a preregistered paired evaluation (N=300 pairs) using a shared‑generation protocol; (2) archival release of execution and analysis artifacts; (3) an artifact‑grounded result showing negligible paired improvement on the supplied synthetic benchmark, and a focused discussion of validity and implications.
sections.related_work: Surveys and recent system papers document active research into LLMs for network configuration, intent translation, tool‑augmented agents, and generate→validate→repair patterns. Representative system and survey reports show that tool augmentation (planner‑centric frameworks, ReAct‑style pipelines) and dedicated validators often reduce errors in generated artifacts. However, prior evaluations are heterogeneous in task scope, benchmarks, and validator semantics; head‑to‑head, preregistered paired comparisons isolating verifier marginal benefit under a shared generation protocol are uncommon. Compared with those works, our study contributes a preregistered paired design, a shared‑generation estimand (see Methods), full archival artifacts, and deterministic analysis results that quantify the verifier’s incremental effect on a synthetic intent suite.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and design: We preregistered study cnsmp2026-llm-verifier-predeployment-001 (SHA‑256 recorded above) as a paired confirmatory design with 300 paired intents stratified by difficulty (100 low / 100 medium / 100 high). The preregistration specified a shared_initial candidate generation per pair, condition definitions, at‑most‑one automated repair for guarded episodes, explicit exclusion/missingness rules, and the primary paired binary analysis (exact McNemar equivalent with paired bootstrap CI; B=10000, seed=1729). Execution protocol (frozen): for each intent the runner produced one shared_initial LLM output using gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json). Two deterministic episodes were then derived: baseline = accept the shared_initial (no verifier repair); guarded = run deterministic_netops_validator_v5 on shared_initial and, if it failed, invoke at most one automated repair call and then revalidate. Success = verifier returns valid==true and no automated_flag under the preregistered full_intent_constraint_validation rule. Justification and implications of shared_initial protocol: the shared_initial protocol was a preregistered design choice intended to isolate verifier+repair effect conditional on a single candidate (it measures the deterministic safety‑net and repair effect given the same LLM proposal). This contrasts with designs that draw independent LLM samples per condition; therefore our estimand does not capture between‑condition generation variance or differences that would arise from independent LLM re‑sampling. This choice focuses inference on the verifier’s ability to deterministically flag and (when permitted) repair an existing candidate rather than on the combined effect of differing generation draws. Sampling and exclusions: pairs are excluded only when both condition calls fail due to provider/infrastructure outage; no exclusions occurred. Analysis: primary confirmatory test implemented by paired_binary_analysis_v1 (exact_mcnemar_two_sided with paired bootstrap percentile CI; B=10000, bootstrap_seed=1729). All seeds, executors, and exclusion rules were frozen and are archived.
sections.results: Execution accounting (artifact-backed): planned_episode_count=600, completed_episode_count=600, complete_pair_count=300, model_calls_used=301, stage_counts: shared_initial_generation=300, repair=1 (execution_manifest.json; deterministic_reconciliation.json). Marginal outcomes (analysis/condition_summary.csv): baseline successes 299/300 (0.9966667), guarded successes 300/300 (1.0). Paired contingency (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv): n11=299, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0. Confirmatory inference (paired_binary_analysis_v1): absolute paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.0033333; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; 95% paired bootstrap percentile CI = [0.00, 0.01] (bootstrap_seed=1729, B=10000). Per‑stratum results: stratification was implemented as preregistered (100 pairs per stratum); observed marginal passes by stratum were baseline: low 100/100, medium 100/100, high 99/100; guarded: 100/100 each (total 300/300). The single discordant (n10=1) occurred in the high complexity stratum and—per the preregistered guarded procedure—was resolved by the single permitted automated repair, producing a guarded pass where baseline failed. Artifact availability for discordant case: the analysis artifacts and reconciliation record document the single discordant count and global repair stage_count=1 (analysis and execution manifests). The low‑level repair provider trace that would show the exact repair prompt and intermediate model‑provider exchange is included in the archived run bundle under the execution manifest; however, a human‑readable repair transcript suitable for inline paper reproduction is not present among the representative examples included in the supplied manuscript evidence excerpt. Consequently we report that the rescued discordant episode exists and is recorded in the archive (paired contingency and provider‑call accounting), but we do not reproduce a verbatim repair prompt/trace in this paper because the supplied representative artifacts in the evidence excerpt do not contain a repair_applied transcript to quote. Contamination and checks: analysis/contamination_summary.csv reports no contamination flags; deterministic_reconciliation reports no cross‑condition cache reuse and all deterministic consistency checks passed. Missingness/exclusions: none.
sections.discussion: Interpretation: On the supplied synthetic suite and with gpt-5-mini, single‑shot generation largely satisfied the deterministic validator (299/300), leaving minimal headroom for the guarded pipeline to improve the preregistered estimand. The observed paired improvement (0.33 percentage points) is operationally small and not significant under the preregistered test because of the ceiling effect and very low discordance. This outcome illustrates that measurable verifier utility (for the paired estimand studied) depends strongly on base LLM capability, task difficulty, and validator coverage. Practical implications: deterministic validators remain valuable for auditability, deterministic flagging, and as a safety net that can rescue some unsafe proposals (the single guarded‑only pass demonstrates such rescue in this run). However, when base model outputs already meet validator checks, measured marginal improvement by the guarded pipeline can be negligible. Threats to validity: Construct validity — our synthetic task generator and deterministic validator share high‑level intent semantics; although contamination instrumentation found no evidence of trivial coupling, alignment between generator and validator reduces task hardness relative to heterogeneous real‑world intents. External validity — a single model (gpt-5-mini) and a single validator were evaluated; results may differ for weaker models or different validators. Estimand scope — the shared_initial protocol (preregistered) conditions inference on the same LLM candidate and therefore does not measure the verifier’s effect when independent generation draws differ by condition. Ceiling effect and power — baseline near‑ceiling performance limited ability to detect large absolute improvements relative to the preregistered 10 percentage‑point target. Recommendations: future work should test weaker models, multiple verifier designs, and more diverse/real operator corpora; evaluate independent‑draw designs if the objective is to measure end‑to‑end pipeline differences that include generation variability; and report operational costs (latency and model‑call budgets) alongside correctness metrics.
sections.conclusion: We report a preregistered, artifact‑archived paired comparison of a verifier‑assisted pipeline versus LLM‑only single‑shot generation for pre‑deployment NetOps changes. Using gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 on a synthetic topology suite, baseline single‑shot generation achieved 299/300 unflagged verifier passes and the guarded pipeline 300/300, producing a negligible paired improvement (0.00333; exact McNemar p=1.0; 95% CI [0.00,0.01]). The preregistered pilot (n=60) was not executed and the main N=300 was used as pre‑specified. These archived results do not imply verifiers are unnecessary; rather, they show that measurable incremental benefit depends on model capability, task difficulty, validator coverage, and the chosen estimand (here, the shared_initial conditional effect). We release full preregistration, execution, and analysis artifacts to support community follow‑up under more challenging and diverse conditions.

limitations: Synthetic benchmark: tasks and topologies were generated by the preregistered deterministic task generator; real‑world heterogeneity may expose different failure modes and increase verifier marginal utility.
Single model and validator: only gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 were evaluated; results may not generalize to other LLMs or richer/verifier‑diverse validators.

Ceiling effect: baseline single‑shot performance was near 100% on this suite (299/300), producing limited discordance and low power to detect small absolute improvements relative to the preregistered target (10 percentage points).
Pilot not executed: the preregistered pilot (n=60) intended for discordance estimation and power calibration was not executed; the main N=300 was used as pre‑specified.
Estimand conditioning: the shared_initial protocol conditions the estimand on a single LLM candidate and therefore does not measure verifier benefit when independent LLM draws per condition differ.

Representative repair transcript unavailable in supplied excerpt: analysis and reconciliation artifacts document the single discordant count and a single repair stage (repair=1), but the supplied representative artifact excerpt does not include a repair_applied transcript suitable for inline reproduction; the rescued episode is recorded in the archive and can be inspected in the full artifact bundle accompanying this submission.
